fact: La Nation states that article 576 of the Code du numerique provides five years' imprisonment and a FCFA 25 million fine for publishing online, without consent, a montage of a person's image or words whose artificial character is not evident or flagged.
Forum on Information and Democracy and ALCRER state that Benin has no specific, sufficiently binding AI regulation or liability regime for AI uses, and no specific AI regulatory authority.

Benin's national digital investigations centre (CNIN) reminded on 29 May 2026 that using AI to alter, generate or share a person's image without consent is punishable under article 576 of the Digital Code by up to five years in prison and a fine of FCFA 25 million.

Levellers says Benin's Digital Code (Loi 2017-20, promulgated 20 April 2018, amended 2021) regulates profiling and automated individual decisions (Article 401) and requires impact assessments for high-risk automated processing, the only binding rules touching AI harms.
A University of Abomey-Calavi law lecturer, presenting to MPs on 12 January 2024, lists artificial intelligence among the missed appointments of the Code du numerique, which does not address it.

Benin's authorities invoked article 576 of the Digital Code in force, which punishes fraudulent manipulation of a third person's image with up to five years in prison and a 25,000,000 CFA franc fine, against AI-generated defamatory images.

Under the supervision of the National Digital Investigations Centre (CNIN), several people were arrested in the days before 27 June 2026 for using AI tools to manipulate images and spread false information.

Actus du Bénin reports that article 576 of Benin's Digital Code provides up to five years in prison and a fine up to CFA 25 million for malicious use of editing applications to alter photographs, audio or video.
Actus du Bénin reports that TikToker Fresnel was arrested and held in custody in June 2026 after posting an AI-generated image of former president Patrice Talon.

Benin's media regulator HAAC, in decision n°26-003 of 3 March 2026 for the 12 April presidential election, requires media to refrain from manipulating information or candidates' words through uncontrolled and irresponsible use of AI, with disciplinary or administrative sanctions for violations.

Benin's media regulator HAAC, in decision N°25-083 of 9 December 2025 for the 11 January 2026 elections, formally bans manipulating statements or information through uncontrolled and irresponsible AI use, with sanctions up to suspension from the campaign for non-compliant outlets.
